report_name: Apollo Global Management Discloses Data Breach via Social Engineering

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: Attackers used voice calls (vishing) to impersonate IT staff, building rapport and urgency to manipulate employees.

attack_patterns.name: Impersonation
attack_patterns.description: The core of the attack was the successful impersonation of trusted internal IT helpdesk personnel to deceive employees.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Attackers gained unauthorized access to company cloud platforms by tricking employees into granting access, thereby using legitimate user credentials or sessions.

campaigns.name: Social Engineering Campaign Targeting Financial Firms
campaigns.description: A social engineering and voice phishing (vishing) campaign where attackers impersonate IT helpdesk staff to trick employees at major financial firms into granting unauthorized access to cloud platforms.

identities.name: Apollo Global Management
identities.description: A global asset manager that suffered a data breach due to a social engineering campaign, resulting in the compromise of employee and client PII.

identities.name: Millennium Management
identities.description: A financial firm reported as a target of a helpdesk impersonation campaign similar to the one that breached Apollo Global Management.

identities.name: Citadel
identities.description: A financial firm reported as a target of a helpdesk impersonation campaign similar to the one that breached Apollo Global Management.

indicators.name: Anomalous MFA Security Info Registration
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous MFA Security Info Registration
id: 2b1a987c-5d6e-4f3a-8b9c-0d1e2f3a4b5c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects when a user registers a new MFA security method (e.g., phone, authenticator app). This is a high-risk activity that was a key part of the social engineering campaign against Apollo, where attackers tricked users into registering attacker-controlled devices.
references:
  - https://gbhackers.com/apollo-global-management-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-23
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.t1656
level: medium
logsource:
  product: azure
  service: auditlogs
detection:
  selection:
    OperationName: 'User registered security info'
    Result: 'success'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the registration of a new MFA security method, a high-risk event that could indicate an attacker tricking a user into adding an attacker-controlled device, as seen in the Apollo breach.
